definition: A reinforcement learning algorithm that constrains policy updates to stay within a limited range of the previous policy, improving training stability.
details: PPO is one of the most widely used RL algorithms for fine-tuning language models via RLHF, valued for its relative simplicity and stability compared to earlier policy gradient methods.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Proximal Policy Optimization.
